decisions.reason: As a bread close to the core range, it is cheap to continue, uncertainty should already be largely resolved, and absent clear negative evidence a traditional bakery would usually retain a proven everyday loaf.
A sweet pastry fits the established confectionery business closely, uses existing craft capabilities, and with no sign of failure the option value still favors keeping it in the assortment.

This farmhouse bread also matches the core offer, but because it overlaps with other bread variants in a medium-sized assortment it faces a somewhat higher rationalization risk even though keeping it remains more likely.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen has a strong positive signal from the gold award, fits the firm's seasonal specialty identity, and can be kept at relatively low incremental cost.

The premium Christmas stollen likewise received a gold award and supports the firm's heritage-led seasonal business, so real-options logic points to retaining it unless later sales clearly disappoint.
